title: Representation Invariance and Allocation: When Subgroup Balance Matters
religious_groups: Religion (as a general category, comparing comments that mention religion vs. those that do not)
findings: The paper's primary finding is that a model's performance sensitivity to the proportion of subgroup data in its training set is highly correlated with the degree of separation of that subgroup in the pre-trained model's latent representation space. For the 'Religion' subgroup in the Civil_comments dataset, this means the toxicity classifier's performance was more affected by the amount of training data mentioning religion when the model had learned to represent 'religious' and 'non-religious' comments very differently.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the sensitivity of a model's performance on toxic comment classification to the allocation of training data containing religious mentions. It specifically analyzed how the model's accuracy on comments mentioning religion changed as the proportion of such comments in the fine-tuning dataset was varied.
